title: benchmark-lab: add representative workload runners, profiling baselines, and reporting pipeline v10
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes:
- Add representative workload runners for common latency/throughput profiles
- Add profiling baselines and serialized profiles for nightly regression detection
- Wire reporting pipeline v2 to surface regression alerts and model/quantization metadata
- Add docs and CI job for nightly benchmark runs
description:
Context and motivation: The benchmark lab currently lacks a standard set of representative workload runners and serialized profiling baselines that we can run nightly and use for automated regression detection. This PR adds a collection of representative runners (small/medium/large sequences, chat-like multi-turn workloads, and embedding throughput tests), stores profiling baselines (CPU/GPU memory & per-token latency histograms), and extends the reporting pipeline to include regression scoring and metadata tagging (model variant, quantization config, sequence distribution).

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Adds new runners under benchmark-lab/runners/ that implement the canonical request shapes used by product teams (chat_multi_turn_runner, generation_long_seq_runner, embeddings_throughput_runner).
- Adds profiling baseline artifacts under benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/ (serialized histograms + meta YAML) and tools to update baselines.
- Adds a nightly CI cron job (ci/cron-jobs/benchmark-nightly.yml) to run the runners and push results to the reporting pipeline.
- Extends reporting/pipeline/reporting_v2.py to ingest baseline artifacts, compute regression deltas, and emit alertable regression events with tags for model/version/quantization.
- Adds lightweight docs and a developer guide at docs/benchmark-lab/README.md describing how to run runners locally and add new workloads.

review_conversation:
Talia: Please add an explainer for how we choose sequence-length buckets and why we prefer histogram baselines vs single-value thresholds.
Aisha: Added docs + inline comments in baseline manager to explain bucket boundaries and histogram aggregation approach (see benchmark-lab/profiling/README section).

Marco: The long-sequence runner was allocating a lot of GPU memory on a couple of model configs; can you reduce the batch accounting to avoid OOMs when running many variants in parallel? Also add a guard to skip GPU-heavy tests on small machine types.
Aisha: Reduced in-flight batch memory and added a --max-parallel flag; updated CI to run GPU tests only on the dedicated GPU runner image. Pushed commit to address.

Evan: The e2e smoke test failed on first CI run (bench_runner_integration) and showed a flaky timing expectation. Can we relax the assertion and add a retry in test harness?
Aisha: Relaxed timing window and added a single retry for bench_runner_integration; re-ran CI and all checks passed.

Approvals: Marco Li approved after memory/parallel changes; Talia approved after docs/baseline explanation; Evan approved after fixing flaky test.

merge_notes: Merged via squash after approvals and green CI. The merge includes the serialized baseline artifacts (benchmarks/profiling/baselines/*) — these are ~3MB total and tracked in LFS-aware path. No infra migrations required.
